stage1.impression: A dark, wide shot down a long bar at night. The bright spectrum-lit bar front and a violet slat wall pull the eye, while the middle of the room is a murky brown cave. There is no product to find: two tall, dull brown-violet boxes in mid-room read as pillars or lecterns, a large flat mauve ceiling takes up the top third, and the dark empty floor takes up the bottom third. It reads as a competent but underlit archviz render, not a magazine interior.

blocking_9: The Atmosphere speakers must read at a glance as tinted acrylic with light passing through them; right now the two in mid-room (x 340-440 and 695-810) have a median luminance of about 10 and no visible tint, batts or horn
The image is far too dark: 70.7% of pixels are below 40, and the floor and middle ground (200-1000, 550-800) have a median of 14
A strong red-brown cast lies over every neutral surface (floor median R35 G8 B7); the concrete and stone need to read as near-neutral grey with coloured light on them, not as rust
The ceiling membrane is a flat, featureless mauve field over the top 30% of the frame and is the brightest large area, so it outweighs the room
The bar panels' saturated green and blue (x 0-100: G128 at median lum 101) shout over the calm kissa idea and over the speakers
The floor has no reflections or texture to carry the room's coloured light toward the camera; it is a uniform dark plane
There are no people or props at the bar to give scale and life

defects.what: Left Atmosphere speaker reads as a dull brown box (lum median 10.6, R26 G6 B4); its acrylic, colour and horn are unreadable
Right Atmosphere speaker reads as a faint violet pillar (lum median 9.7); the 150 W spot does not reach it, or is far too weak
Lounge chairs and the record-player zone in front of the record wall are crushed (median 5.6, 9.6% crushed); Cumulus is invisible
Record-wall spots make three bright, repeating arch pools that compete with the speakers
Ceiling membrane is a large flat mauve field (median 59) with a visible hard-edged elliptical boundary; it reads as CG
Floor is a uniform dark red-brown plane (median 14, R35 G8 B7) with no texture, no reflections and no light pools; a third of the frame is dead
Bar panels are oversaturated, flat emissive colour blocks (green median lum 101) that read as an LED sign
Booths are a mass of dark red upholstery; the booth Bell lamps glow faintly and light nothing
Street window reads as dark, blank panels with grey rectangles; there is no street life or depth beyond it
A red/magenta colour cast across the whole frame; there is no neutral reference anywhere

changes.problem: The speakers are the products and they are invisible: no light passes through their acrylic, so they read as dull boxes.

evidence.measured: lum median 10.6, p95 32.1, R26 G6 B4; the right one (695-810) has median 9.7

change.setting: lamps: spots on each Fog speaker (and add a narrow top-down spot on each mid-room speaker, aimed into the cabinet so the batts glow through the tint)
change.to: 900 W, cone 25 deg, aimed at the cabinet's centre from above and behind

changes.expected: Each mid-room speaker glows in its own tint with visible white batts and a bright horn rim, and is the brightest object in the middle third

changes.problem: The frame is underexposed overall and the middle ground is a cave.

evidence.measured: lum median 14.1; 70.7% of the whole frame is below 40

changes.expected: Floor and mid-room come up to a readable low-key level while the highlights stay below clipping

changes.problem: A heavy red cast makes the concrete and stone read as rust and muddies every speaker tint.

evidence.measured: R35 G8 B7 on what should be a near-neutral concrete floor

change.to: about 3000 K (neutralise the warm sources), tint +5 toward green; set it so the floor reads grey-warm, not red

changes.expected: The floor reads as warm grey concrete, and the coloured light from the bar and slats reads as colour on a neutral ground

changes.problem: The back-lit ceiling membrane is the largest bright field and draws the eye away from the room.

evidence.measured: lum median 58.7 (p5 53.8) mauve, more than four times the floor's median of 14

changes.expected: The ceiling falls to a dark, quiet canopy and the eye drops into the room and onto the speakers

changes.problem: The bar panels are saturated LED blocks that shout over the calm brief and outshine the products.

evidence.measured: lum median 101, G128; the blue panel (200-320, 420-470) reaches p95 152

changes.expected: The panels glow softly in spectrum order and stay below the speakers' luminance

changes.problem: The floor is a dead, uniform plane that wastes a third of the frame and carries none of the room's light.

evidence.measured: lum_range 17.8 (p5 6.6, p95 24.4); the falloff toward the camera is flat at 14-16

change.to: honed, sealed polished concrete: roughness 0.25, a fine aggregate bump map at 2-5 mm scale, a mid-grey base colour

changes.expected: Soft, blurred coloured reflections of the bar panels, the slats and the speakers run across the floor toward the camera, leading the eye into the room

changes.problem: The record-wall spots make three repeating bright arches that compete with the speakers, while the lounge and Cumulus below them are crushed.

evidence.measured: lum median 5.6, crush 9.6%; the record wall above (460-745, 280-390) has p95 127.6

change.setting: spots on each corner speaker; DJ desk lamp
change.to: spots re-aimed down onto the corner speakers, not the record wall, and widened to a softer edge (blend 0.6); DJ desk 250 W

changes.expected: The record wall becomes an even, warm backdrop, and the lounge chairs and Cumulus emerge from black

changes.problem: The room is empty and lifeless, with nothing at human scale at the bar or in the booths.

evidence.measured: the booth region is a dark red mass; the booth Bells glow but light nothing

change.to: two or three seated, slightly motion-blurred figures at the bar and one booth, glasses and a menu on the bar top, a light haze in the air at density 0.005; booth Bells at 70 W

changes.expected: The frame reads as a lived-in bar at night, with scale cues and atmospheric depth toward the record wall

out_of_scope.request: A speaker tint lighter or more saturated than Smoke or Fog for the two mid-room speakers, so they read against the dark wood
out_of_scope.why: The colour of each speaker is fixed; only light can make the tint read

out_of_scope.request: Move the two mid-room speakers so they are not silhouetted against the dark wood panels
